stem: A registrar assumes that most sexually active adolescents feel positive after sex unless there is a pregnancy scare, so emotional impact does not need to be asked about routinely. Which response best matches the notes?

options.text: That is reasonable, because adolescents usually report feeling good after sex
That is reasonable, because emotional impact matters only when sex is non-consensual
That is reasonable, because wellbeing concerns are separate from risky sexual behaviour
That is not well supported, because only about half report feeling good after intercourse and risky sexual behaviour can affect mental health and wellbeing
That is not well supported, but only because HIV knowledge in adolescents is poor

explanation: That is not well supported. Only about half of adolescents report feeling good after intercourse, and risky sexual behaviour can affect mental health and wellbeing, so emotional impact should be asked about routinely.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

rationale: The notes do not support assuming sexual experiences are usually emotionally positive. Wellbeing and pleasure are relevant parts of adolescent sexual health assessment. Risky sexual behaviour includes impacts on mental health and wellbeing.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because the notes do not support assuming most adolescents feel good after sex.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because emotional impact matters beyond non-consensual situations alone.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because the notes explicitly include mental health and wellbeing within risky sexual behaviour.
optionExplanations.D: Correct because only about half report feeling good after intercourse, and risky sexual behaviour can affect mental health and wellbeing.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because the HIV-knowledge point is unrelated to the emotional-impact issue here.
